clips.send: Light bulb (load). Changes electrical energy into light and heat. The thin tungsten filament has high resistance. Current heats it until it glows. More current through a bulb means more power, so it glows brighter. In series, bulbs share the battery’s voltage, so each gets less and they are dimmer. In parallel, every bulb gets the full battery voltage, so each is as bright as a single bulb alone.

clips.send: Switch. Opens or closes the path. A closed switch completes the loop, so current flows. An open switch leaves an air gap. Air is an insulator, so the current stops everywhere in that loop at once. In a parallel circuit, each branch can have its own switch, like the light switches in each room of your home. Click any switch on the board to flip it.

clips.send: Electrons (moving charge). Tiny negative charges that flow in metal wires. The blue dots are electrons. They flow from the minus terminal, through the circuit, to the + terminal. Scientists draw “conventional current” the other way, from + to minus . That rule was chosen before electrons were discovered. The dots move faster when the current is bigger. Real electrons drift slowly, but the whole wire is full of them, so they all start moving together and the bulb lights instantly.

clips.send: Wire (conductor). Gives the current a path. Copper is a good conductor: its electrons move easily from atom to atom. The plastic coating is an insulator. It keeps the current inside the wire and protects you. Current flows only when there is a complete, unbroken loop: a closed circuit. If a wire connects the battery’s terminals with nothing else in the path, that is a short circuit. The current is huge and the wire gets dangerously hot.

clips.send: Ammeter. Measures current in amperes (A). Current is how much charge flows past a point each second, measured in amperes (amps, A). An ammeter is connected in series, right in the path of the current. Ohm’s law: current equals voltage divided by resistance (I equals V divided by R). In parallel, the total current from the battery is the sum of the branch currents.

clips.send: Battery (cells). The energy source that pushes charges around the loop. Voltage, measured in volts (V), is the “push” a battery gives to charges. Each cell here gives 1.5 V. Cells joined end-to-end (in series) add up: 3 cells equals 4.5 V. Inside the battery, chemical energy is changed into electrical energy. Electrons leave the negative ( minus ) terminal, travel around the circuit, and return to the positive (+) terminal.

clips.send: 小灯泡（用电器）。把电能转化为光能和内能（热）。细细的钨丝电阻很大，电流把它加热到发光。通过灯泡的电流越大，功率越大，灯泡就越亮。串联时，各个灯泡分享电池的电压，每个分到的少，所以较暗。并联时，每个灯泡都得到电池的全部电压，所以每个都和单独一个灯泡一样亮。

clips.send: 电子（移动的电荷）。在金属导线中流动的带负电的微粒。蓝色小点代表电子，它们从负极出发，经过电路流向正极。科学上规定的“电流方向”正好相反，是从正极流向负极，这是在发现电子之前就定下的规定。电流越大，小点移动得越快。真实的电子移动得很慢，但导线里到处都是电子，它们同时开始移动，所以灯泡一接通就亮。

clips.send: 开关。断开或接通电路。闭合的开关让回路完整，电流就能流动。断开的开关留下一段空气间隙。空气是绝缘体，所以整个回路里的电流会同时停止。在并联电路中，每条支路都可以有自己的开关，就像家里每个房间各有一个电灯开关。点击电路板上的任意开关来切换它。

clips.send: 电池（电池组）。电源：推动电荷在电路中流动。电压的单位是伏特（V），它是电池对电荷的“推力”。这里每节电池提供 1.5 V。电池首尾相连（串联）时电压相加：3 节 等于 4.5 V。电池内部把化学能转化为电能。电子从负极（减） 出发，沿电路流动，再回到正极（+）。
clips.text: 电池（电池组）. 电源：推动电荷在电路中流动. 电压的单位是伏特（V），它是电池对电荷的“推力”。. 这里每节电池提供 1.5 V。电池首尾相连（串联）时电压相加：3 节 = 4.5 V。. 电池内部把化学能转化为电能。. 电子从负极（−） 出发，沿电路流动，再回到正极（+）。

clips.send: 电流表。测量电流，单位是安培（A）。电流表示每秒通过导线某一截面的电荷有多少，单位是安培（安，A）。电流表要串联在电路中，让电流从它里面流过。欧姆定律：电流 等于 电压 除以 电阻（I 等于 U 除以 R）。并联电路中，干路的总电流等于各支路电流之和。
clips.text: 电流表. 测量电流，单位是安培（A）. 电流表示每秒通过导线某一截面的电荷有多少，单位是安培（安，A）。. 电流表要串联在电路中，让电流从它里面流过。. 欧姆定律：电流 = 电压 ÷ 电阻（I = U ÷ R）。. 并联电路中，干路的总电流等于各支路电流之和。

clips.send: 导线（导体）。为电流提供通路。铜是良好的导体，它的电子很容易在原子之间移动。外面的塑料皮是绝缘体，它让电流只在导线里流动，也保护我们的安全。只有形成完整、没有断开的回路（闭合电路），电流才会流动。如果导线直接把电池两极连起来、中间没有用电器，就是短路。电流非常大，导线会变得很烫，非常危险。
